children: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's team informed Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he planned to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors, according to Brian Mast (R., Fla.), the chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. Mast said the sides were negotiating on the date of Huang's testimony.

It's unclear whether Huang's resignation on Thursday will change his calculus about whether to testify. Mast told The Wall Street Journal that the resignation didn't affect the committee's expectation that he testify. The congressman previously threatened to subpoena Huang if he didn't comply with their request.

The communication from Huang's team came in response to a letter from Mast and two other House Republicans requesting testimony from Huang about his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence source.

Mast separately told reporters that Huang could testify in a week and that the "parameters" of the negotiations with Huang's team focus in part on whether the testimony would be under oath and include a transcribed interview.
